producedBy: Captain, from a read-only audit lane's diff reading, with every decisive claim re-measured independently before it was recorded here
question: For each first-cohort candidate, does any change made after the decision owner's completed-output approval fall in the class that requires a NEW decision, or is it all in the class the existing approval already covers?
howTheTestWorks: The decision record carries its own two lists. correctionsNotRequiringANewLegalDecision covers renderer wiring, field mapping, PDF flattening, active-content removal, text fitting, caption correction, a source hash refresh for the same form and revision, visual fixes, storage integration, route-to-family wiring, packet-builder wiring and deterministic fixture corrections. requiresANewDecisionOwnerDecision covers changing the remedy, eligibility logic, a mandatory filing, venue, the required recipient or service party, replacing a mandatory official form with a custom pleading, and adding substantive legal language not already present in the approved design. A change is read against those lists and nothing else.
whyAnUnchangedPacketProofIsNotEnough: For the original three candidates, packetProofSha256 and legalDesignMemoSha256 are unchanged since the approval, and that is necessary rather than sufficient. Those packet proofs attest implementation outputs under src/lib/rcap/packets/jurisdictions/ and scripts/verify-rcap-*-custom-pleading.mjs, and none of those paths exists in this checkout — the shipping artifacts come from the census-v1 generator instead. The proofs are unchanged because nothing touched them, not because they describe what now ships. So coverage was decided by reading the rendered output against the unchanged legal design memo, not by trusting the proof hash.
method: For the original three candidates, each legal design memo was flattened into a string corpus, every memo fragment of thirty characters or more was removed from the normalised text of the rendered canonical fixture and the participant instructions, and the residue of sixty characters or more was read by hand. For the 2026-09-04 Georgia expansion, the exact post-approval path history, approved memo and manifest, later route contract, instructions, field map, build findings and both four-page fixture PDFs were read in full; hashes and page counts were re-measured and every PDF page was visually inspected. COVERED is recorded only when that evidence places every post-approval delta on the owner's existing-approval list.

families.decisiveEvidence: The approved ga-rfo memo says outputStrategy process_guidance and states that no petition is generated pending later counsel approval of a distinct post-consent stage. The later route contract says outcomeMode participant_packet and names a separate petition family and components. The current guidance assembly does not pretend to be that petition, but it imports one additional substantive stop from the later contract — 'A contested evidentiary hearing leaves self-help' — which is not among the approved ga-rfo track's four selfHelpStopConditions. That addition is useful and plausibly correct; condition seven asks whether it is already approved, and the owner's own list says substantive legal language not already present in the approved design requires a new decision.

the ga-rfo object in GA.memo.json, the derived process-guidance specification, participant-instructions.md, production-field-map.json, build-findings.json and the complete post-approval history of every changed family path were read against the owner's two lists
the legal-design memo and packet-proof hashes recompute exactly to the values in the approval manifest

families.whyTheFamilyApprovalDoesNotOpenTheRoute: The present family remains guidance-only and its completed-output approval does not extend to the separate petition family the runtime route requires. This audit creates no route verdict, no fulfilment record and no commercial authority.
families.consequence: Keep GA:retroactive-first-offender-treatment-under-42-8-66 closed. A decision owner must approve the post-approval legal delta, and a different lane must still perform the pending route-specific fifteen-obligation verification before any exact fulfilment record could be considered.

families.decisiveEvidence: The approved design defers to a mandatory, exclusive official form and the built packet does not carry it. The SC memo states for every route that the composed package 'is not a substitute for the official order form', that section 17-22-930 makes the solicitor's blank form 'mandatory and to the exclusion of all other expungement forms', and it declares a required component official_form_reference naming SCCA 223A1 GS (Revised 04/2026).
measuredIndependentlyByCaptain: the string 223A1 appears in no file in the family directory and nowhere in the rendered canonical fixture; the only form named in the packet is SCCA 223C, on one route
the rendered componentSet contains no official_form_reference, no records_checklist and no fee_instrument_schedule component on any route
eleven of the twelve tracks in the SC memo carry destination.kind prosecutor, and the rendered packet is captioned IN THE ......... COURT
families.whyTheAmbiguityResolvesAgainstCoverage: The participant instructions do carry the memo's filing rule and name the solicitor's office, so the packet is not silent about it everywhere. But the phrase 'Filing as recorded:' appears zero times in any of the three PDFs — the composer drops that rule from the rendered packet — so a participant holding only the PDF never learns the mandatory form exists. Attaching the owner's approval to that would extend it past what it says.
alsoFlagged: sc_pti_17_22_150 is named in the manifest family row and in the memo but is not built; the family delivers ten of eleven approved tracks

build-findings.json asserts that no official form was substituted while its own first finding records sourceStatus CUSTOM_PLEADING_FROM_CODIFIED_TEXT and the master queue row reads SOURCE_BOUND_BY_HELD_BYTES with custody SOURCE_GENUINELY_MISSING
families.consequence: This is not only a cohort-scope question. A mandatory-exclusive official form that the approved design requires and the packet omits is a packet defect, so the family is sent for an independent re-read on COMPONENT_SET, FILING_DESTINATION and ROUTE_IDENTITY rather than left proven.

grantsNothing: This audit decides which families a pre-existing approval already covers. It creates no approval, opens no route, sets no price, and changes no family state by itself.
